title: Dutch Andrus, Circle hall and the Covington boat
summary: He played with Dutch Andrus at Woodman of the World Hall and on the boat to Madisonville and Covington for private parties.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Working the Streckfus riverboats with Fate Marable

blocks.x: Do you remember some of the jobs you played in different places, aside from parties?

Well, I remember playing at the Woodman of the World Hall, a place called Circle. It was an open-air place. We played there four nights a week. Dutch Andrus' band. And I played on the boat a lot with Dutch. And I used to go over and play in Covington. There was a boat that used to operate from New Orleans to Madisonville. And the name of the boat was in Madisonville. And I think at the same time there was one in operation by the name of the Susquehanna. And we had...
Remember the Camellia, too? Was there one called the Camellia? Was that the same?

I seem to recall that, but not in the same connection. I think that was a boat that was rented out for parties. I think they used to rent it out for parties. Seeming as if it was a yacht. Now, I might be wrong, but it seemed like it was a... The Camellia was a yacht, but I stand to be corrected on that point. But we used to go to Covington to play for private parties. People would hire us to come over. And as soon as we'd get on the boat, we'd start playing. Just out of goodness of our hearts and for the love of it. We didn't expect any money. We didn't get any. The only money we got was when we got to Covington and played. These people would meet us at Madisonville rather than take us to Covington in their automobile. And we'd play our job and stay at their home. And next day we'd get the boat and come back to New Orleans. Is there dancing on the boat? Oh yeah. As soon as we unpacked those instruments, there was dancing. And on the way back, it'd be a repeat performance.
